issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem 4.1 attempts to establish the inf-sup condition for the full multilinear form \tilde{A}_h by treating the boundary flux term as a perturbation of A_h, whose inf-sup constant is denoted \beta. However, A_h and the norm \|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h} both depend explicitly on \gamma. In the step bounding \|v_h\|_{\mathrm{d},h}, the proof drops \gamma by writing \|p_h\|^2 + \gamma h^{-1} \|(v - v_h)\cdot n\|^2 \lesssim \|p_h\|^2. In reality, \|v_h\|_{\mathrm{d},h} \le C\sqrt{1+\gamma}\|p_h\|_{0,h}, which forces the inf-sup constant \beta of A_h to decay as O(\gamma^{-1/2}) as \gamma \to \infty. Consequently, both \beta - \alpha and 1/(4\alpha\gamma) are of order O(\gamma^{-1/2}), so taking \gamma large cannot be assumed to make (\beta - \alpha - 1/(4\alpha\gamma)) positive. Furthermore, setting \gamma = 2/\beta^2 is circular because \beta depends directly on \gamma.

failure_location.quote: Choosing $\alpha < \beta$ and assuming $\gamma$ is sufficiently large so that $\left(\beta - \alpha -\frac{1}{4 \alpha \gamma}\right) > 0$, we obtain the discrete inf-sup condition for $\tilde A_h$. For instance, taking $\alpha=\frac{\beta}{2}$ and $\gamma = \frac{2}{\beta^2}$ yields the inf-sup constant $\tilde{\beta}=\beta/4$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rework the stability proof to construct a combined test function (e.g. testing with (u_h + \delta v_p, p_h + \dots)) that controls coercivity, inf-sup stability, and the boundary penalty term simultaneously without uncoupling \beta from \gamma.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete stability guarantee (discrete inf-sup condition) for the discrete system with weakly imposed flux boundary conditions is unsupported as written. Theorem 5.2, which directly invokes the stability constant \tilde{\beta}, also becomes unestablished.
issues.title: Circular parameter dependency in inf-sup proof for weakly imposed flux conditions
issues.why_classification: Stability of Nitsche/penalty weak boundary conditions for mixed problems is standardly provable through a coupled test-function argument, which requires a contained nontrivial proof revision rather than abandoning the formulation or its guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The interpolation estimates for $u$, $\dv{u}$ and $p$, together with the trace inequality for the boundary term in $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$ and Assumption~\ref{as:extensions}, then prove the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 5.2 claims that the squared error \|u - u_h\|_{\mathrm{d},h}^2 converges at rate O(h^{2r}) when u \in H^r(\Omega). However, the definition of \|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h}^2 contains the boundary penalty term \gamma h^{-1} \|(u - u_h)\cdot n\|_{L^2(\Gamma_u)}^2. Since \Gamma_u is an unfitted boundary cutting through background elements, the trace inequality on cut elements yields h^{-1} \|(u - \Pi_{d,h}(u))\cdot n\|_{L^2(\Gamma_u)}^2 \lesssim h^{-2} \|u - \Pi_{d,h}(u)\|_{L^2}^2 + \|\nabla(u - \Pi_{d,h}(u))\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim h^{2r-2}\|u\|_{H^r}^2 (or O(h^{2r-1}) assuming H^{r+1/2} boundary regularity). In particular, for lowest-order elements (k_u=0, r=1), piecewise constants on cut cells approximating an H^1 normal trace on \Gamma_u have an L^2(\Gamma_u) error of size O(h), meaning h^{-1}\|(u - u_h)\cdot n\|_{L^2(\Gamma_u)}^2 = O(h), not O(h^2). The rate h^{2r} for \|u - u_h\|_{\mathrm{d},h}^2 is therefore mathematically false when \Gamma_u \neq \emptyset.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the error estimate in Theorem 5.2 to state the correct rate for the boundary-penalised norm (O(h^{2r-1}) or O(h^{2r-2}) depending on regularity assumptions on u), or separate the flux error estimate into an L^2(\Omega) estimate of rate O(h^r) and a trace penalty estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The a priori error estimate in the mesh-dependent flux norm \|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h} is overstated by at least half an order (in norm) when \Gamma_u \neq \emptyset. Downstream bounds that couple pressure error directly to \|u - \Pi_{d,h}(u)\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$ also lose asymptotic rate unless stated separately.
issues.title: Sub-optimal convergence rate for the flux energy norm with unfitted flux boundaries
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the boundary penalty component of the mesh-dependent norm restores the estimate while preserving the optimal convergence rate of the bulk L^2 errors and divergence errors.
